title: Tester: venue staff and judge
brief:
Read and follow <scratch> first. You are "judge" (report: judge.md).

Persona: a hackathon judge with 10 minutes, then a venue owner. As the judge: open the address cold. In the first 2 minutes, can you tell what Join is, what is real and what is demo, where to start, and where an AI agent would start? Then do the shortest path to see PayPal doing something real (sandbox), and note how many clicks it took and where you got stuck. Then as the owner of Echo Karaoke: Venue view, sign in as the venue, look at your bookings, money ("What Join brought in"), reconcile, extras, disputes and your negotiation rules; change a rule (e.g. the floor or style) and see if anything confirms it took effect. Judge the wording for a non-technical venue owner. Report everything the shared brief asks, plus a short "first two minutes" paragraph.

Badminton, karaoke, an escape room, board games, a barbecue, hot pot: Join is the marketplace AI agents come to. They find who is free, negotiate the price with the venue, split the cost and settle it with PayPal, inside the limits you set. No agent? Join's website agent asks what you want and does it for you. Join keeps the rules and shows you everything an agent did.

Why not just split it on Venmo afterwards? Because someone has to book and pay first. Here the venue is paid only when the money is real: the organizer guarantees it in PayPal, each friend pays their own share, and anyone who said yes and didn't pay gets a PayPal invoice. Nobody chases anyone.

Connect your agent
Claude, or any MCP or A2A agent, with a token only you can make.
Set your limits
Per booking, per week, which venues. Agents can read them, never change them.
Watch it work
Every search, offer, counter-offer and payment, as it happens.
For AI agents

An agent can use Join from this address alone. Start with /llms.txt: what Join is, how to get in for your person, the tools and the rules.

MCP: http://192.168.31.145:8797/mcp · REST: /api/agent/<tool> · A2A: agent card
A person makes their agent's token on the Connect page; for testing, a demo account can make one too (llms.txt says how).
Limits only the person can set are enforced by Join whatever an agent is told; every step an agent takes is shown to the people involved.

VERDICT: 0 BLOCKER, 0 BUG, 10 CONFUSING

The full report is at `<scratch>`. I did not run a new negotiation after changing Echo Karaoke's rules, so I can't say whether the new rules change the price an agent gets.

**First two minutes.** The headline and paragraph make it clear that Join is an agent marketplace for group plans paid through PayPal. The "For AI agents" box points straight to `/llms.txt`, and a person starts with the first-name box and Start. Real versus demo is only half answered: "made-up town, PayPal sandbox, test money" sits in small grey text below the fold. From the landing page I couldn't tell whether PayPal is actually called or simulated.

**Shortest path to PayPal.** It took 5 clicks: Start, Plan something, a Karaoke chip, Negotiate this, Go ahead. The agent haggled and "PayPal sandbox: $23.40 authorized" appeared in Activity, in about a minute. I got stuck at the next step, which was to see PayPal itself. Nothing in the interface shows an order id, a PayPal link or the real approval.
- The "PayPal sandbox" pill in the sidebar looks clickable and does nothing.
- The raw responses did contain real PayPal order and authorization ids, and a real `sandbox.paypal.com` invoice URL, so something real is happening behind the page.
- The Activity line calls the approval "a demo stand-in for their approval".

**Venue owner (Echo Karaoke).**
- Signing in as the venue takes one click and needs no password. The header still says "Judge", so it isn't clear who I am.
- "What Join brought in" adds up, but it counts only locked bookings. Held bookings worth about $108 are missing from the money cards.
- Reconciliation takes about 6 seconds to load with no spinner. It shows raw ids like `u_6e642aaf2b` and the status "not in transaction reporting yet", and the PayPal fee column is blank.
- Bill extras sent a $12 invoice with no confirmation step. The page then shows "billed $12.00 (sent)" but no link to the invoice.
- Rules saved and persisted after reload, with "Saved. The next negotiation uses these rules." The form doesn't explain how Style, Floor and Counter-offers interact. A floor of 5 gave no visible error (the server rejected it).
- Developer wording appears on owner-facing screens: `list_transactions`, `create_invoice`, AP2, Ed25519 and `qwen2.5:0.5b`.

**Shared-server side effects.** I changed Echo Karaoke's rules and later restored them to Eager / 65 / 3 counter-offers. I also sent a $12 sandbox invoice on booking `bk_59deff6c7833`, which belongs to another tester.

**Three most important findings:**
1. A judge can't see PayPal doing anything real; the pill and labels are text only, and the order id and invoice link never appear on screen.
2. The owner screens are full of developer wording and raw ids, which hides whether the venue was actually paid.
3. Extras and rules give weak feedback: the invoice has no confirmation step and no link, and an invalid floor shows no message.
